Home.title: Atlas
Home.tagline: Source-to-target specifications, structured, validated and approved.

SignIn.title: Sign in to Atlas
SignIn.invalidCredentials: The email or password is incorrect.
SignIn.unavailable: Sign-in is not available right now. Please try again later.

Progress.title: Project progress
Progress.subtitle: Where Atlas stands on its roadmap. Updated on {date}.
Progress.waitingIntro: Only you can do these; each one unblocks a step.

NoAccess.title: No access
NoAccess.body: Your account is suspended or no longer exists. Ask an Admin of your organization if you think this is a mistake.

Errors.noCredit: No license credit remains. Ask Atlas for more licenses, or request the deletion of an account you no longer need.
Errors.emailUnavailable: This e-mail address cannot be used. Use another address.
Errors.lastAdmin: The organization must keep at least one active Admin.
Errors.notYourself: You cannot do this on your own account; another Admin must do it.
Errors.creditsBelowAccounts: Credits cannot go below the number of accounts. The customer must first request deletions.
Errors.minimumCredit: An organization starts with at least 1 credit.
Errors.deletionPending: Cancel the deletion request before reactivating this account.
Errors.forbidden: You are not allowed to do this.
Errors.expiredLink: This link has expired or was already used.
Errors.invalid: Some values are missing or not valid. Check the form and try again.
Errors.unavailable: Atlas cannot do this right now. Please try again in a moment.
Errors.archived: This project is archived: restore it before changing it.
Errors.idTaken: This identifier is already used in this project.
Errors.invalidId: Use lowercase letters, digits, _ and - only.
Errors.domainCode: A domain code has 2 to 5 capital letters or digits.
Errors.domainInUse: This domain is used by models, rules or value mappings: retire it instead.
Errors.notAnAccount: Owner and stewards must be active accounts of your organization.
Errors.unknownDomain: Choose an active domain of your organization.
Errors.nameTaken: A named version with this name already exists in the project.

Projects.title: Projects
Projects.name: Name
Projects.descriptionHint: What the project is for, e.g. “Multi-ERP consolidation 2027”.
Projects.emptyHint: Create the first project of your organization.
Projects.emptyViewer: No project has been shared yet.

Project.problemCounts: {errors, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}} · {warnings, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}
Project.startBody: Describe the systems the project reads (ERP, MES…) and their tables: by hand, or by importing a dictionary file.
Project.comingNext: Models, rules, value mappings, history and downloads arrive in the next steps of this phase.

Accounts.title: Licenses and accounts
Accounts.subtitle: Each account uses one license credit, whatever its status, until its deletion is validated.
Accounts.newDescription: The person receives an e-mail to choose a password. The account uses one credit at once.
Accounts.name: Name
Accounts.suspendBody: They are signed out at once and can no longer open Atlas. The license credit stays used; you can reactivate the account later.
Accounts.deleteBody: The account is suspended at once. Atlas then removes it and gives the credit back. You can cancel the request until then. Their past changes stay in the history with their name.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.name: Name
Profile.sessionsBody: Signs you out of Atlas on every other browser and device.

Invite.title: Join Atlas
Invite.invalid: This invitation link has expired or was already used. Ask the Admin of your organization to send it again.
Invite.intro: You are invited with {email}. Choose your name as colleagues will see it, and a password.
Invite.name: Name

Reset.title: Forgotten password
Reset.intro: Enter the e-mail address of your account. We send you a link to choose a new password.
Reset.expired: This link has expired or was already used. Ask for a new one.
Reset.sent: If an account exists for this address, an e-mail with a link has been sent. Check your inbox.

Control.title: Organizations
Control.subtitle: Licensing figures only: Atlas never shows projects, people or content of a customer.
Control.newDescription: Atlas invites the customer's first Admin by e-mail; the invitation uses the first credit.
Control.name: Name
Control.adminEmailHint: Usually the customer's contact person. The control tower does not keep this address.
Control.inviteFailed: The organization was created, but the invitation of its first Admin could not be sent. Try again below.
Control.creditsHint: At least {accounts}, the number of accounts that exist.
Control.deletionsCount: {count, plural, =0 {No account waits for deletion.} one {# account waits for deletion.} other {# accounts wait for deletion.}}
Control.deletionsHint: Which accounts they are stays with the customer.
Control.validateBody: The accounts are removed for good and their credits go back to the organization.
Control.deletionValidated: 1 account removed; its credit is back.
Control.deletionsValidated: Accounts removed; their credits are back.
Control.firstAdminBody: This organization has no account yet. Invite its first Admin.
Control.auditSubtitle: Every action of the operator, kept for good.

audit.deletions_validated: {count, plural, one {# deletion validated} other {# deletions validated}}

Sources.title: Sources
Sources.subtitle: The systems this project reads and the description of their tables. Metadata only: Atlas never reads your data.
Sources.systemHint: A source system, e.g. one ERP instance. Two instances of the same product are two systems.
Sources.systemIdHint: Lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, e.g. sap_fr. It cannot change later.
Sources.productHint: e.g. SAP S/4HANA 2023, Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2
Sources.landingHint: Where this system's raw data lands in the warehouse; the generated code reads from there.
Sources.deleteSystemBody: The system and its datasets leave the project. They stay in the history and can be restored. Mappings that read them will show errors.
Sources.newDatasetHint: A table, view or file of this system, entered by hand. You fill its columns next.
Sources.datasetNameHint: As in the source, e.g. KNA1.
Sources.copyHint: The systems and their datasets are copied into this project; the copies are then independent.
Sources.datasetCount: {count, plural, =0 {no dataset} one {# dataset} other {# datasets}}
Sources.copiedSome: Copied, except the systems already in this project.
Sources.emptyBody: Add the first system this project reads, then describe its tables by hand or import a dictionary.
Sources.emptyViewer: No source has been described yet.

Dataset.deleteBody: The dataset leaves the project. It stays in the history and can be restored. Mappings that read it will show errors.
Dataset.landingNameHint: Only when it differs from the system's naming pattern.
Dataset.pasteHint: Tip: paste rows copied from a spreadsheet into the grid (column, native type, nullable, key position, description).
Dataset.dialectHint: Used to translate native types into Atlas types.
Dataset.name: Column
Dataset.unknownType: Unknown native type: choose the Atlas type.
Dataset.noColumn: No column yet: add one, or paste rows from a spreadsheet.

Import.title: Import a dictionary
Import.subtitle: Describe many tables at once from a file listing their columns. Only metadata: no data is read.
Import.noSystem: Create a system first: the import fills the datasets of one system.
Import.step1Body: Run the query of your database with your own tools and access, and save the result as CSV (or Excel). Atlas never connects to your systems.
Import.otherSources: Any file with the columns dataset, column, native_type (and optionally nullable, primary_key_position, description, dataset_description, namespace) works, e.g. an export of an ERP data dictionary.
Import.dialectHint: Translates native types into Atlas types.
Import.fileHint: CSV (comma or semicolon) or Excel .xlsx, up to 20 MB. Read in your browser only.
Import.tooLarge: The file is larger than 20 MB.
Import.unreadable: This file cannot be read. Save it as CSV (UTF-8) or Excel .xlsx.
Import.empty: The file has no row under its header.
Import.missingList: Kept, as they are not in the file (never deleted silently): {list}
Import.done: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing changed: the datasets were already up to date.} one {# dataset saved.} other {# datasets saved.}}

Domains.title: Domains
Domains.subtitle: The business processes of your organization (Sales, Manufacture, Govern…), shared by all projects. Each target model, business rule and value mapping belongs to one of them; their stewards approve its objects.
Domains.dialogHint: A business process that owns models, rules and value mappings and is responsible for their meaning.
Domains.codeHint: 2 to 5 capitals or digits, e.g. SEL. It cannot change later.
Domains.name: Name
Domains.stewardsHint: They review and approve the domain's objects (from the review phase). Choose at least one, ideally two.
Domains.emptyBody: Define your organization's business processes first: models, rules and value mappings are assigned to them.
Domains.emptyViewer: Your Admins have not defined the domains yet.

Models.title: Models
Models.subtitle: The target tables of the project, by domain: their columns, where each value comes from, and how branches combine.
Models.newHint: A target table. Start empty, or from a source dataset: its columns become target columns copied from it.
Models.noDomain: Ask an Admin to define your organization's domains first (Organization › Domains): every model belongs to one.
Models.idHint: e.g. dim_customer. It cannot change later.
Models.name: Name
Models.descriptionHint: The business meaning of one row.
Models.grainHint: What one row represents, e.g. one customer of the group.
Models.fromHint: Optional: a source dataset whose columns are copied.
Models.emptyBody: Create the first target table of the project, empty or from a source dataset.
Models.emptyViewer: No model has been written yet.

ModelEditor.deleteBody: The model leaves the project. It stays in the history and can be restored. Models that read it will show errors.
ModelEditor.name: Name
ModelEditor.descriptionHint: The business meaning of one row.
ModelEditor.columnsHint: The contract of the target table, written first: every branch must fill each column (or say why it cannot).

Conditions.incompatible: These types cannot be compared: {left} and {right} (MM-120).

Branches.intro: A branch is one source path into the model, usually one per system: the datasets it reads, how they join, and which rows it keeps.
Branches.label: Label
Branches.datasetsHint: Each dataset gets a short alias used in joins and mappings. The first one drives the grain. A model can be read too (a chain).
Branches.chooseSource: Choose a dataset or a model
Branches.joinsHint: Add a second dataset to join it.
Branches.confirmed: I confirm this many-to-many join is intended: it multiplies rows (MM-121).
Branches.joinDescriptionPlaceholder: Why this join exists, in business words
Branches.groupByHint: When the branch aggregates: every mapping is then a grouping column or ends with an aggregation.

Steps.unstructured: Atlas cannot check its types or lineage.

help.convert: To another type: cast, parse a text, or format.
help.map_values: Through a value mapping of the project.
help.calculate: A function of the catalogue (arithmetic, text, dates).
help.concat: Joins several values; empty parts are skipped.
help.lookup: One value from another dataset, without adding rows.
help.rule: A reusable business rule of the project.
help.sql: Last resort: write SQL, with the reason why it cannot be structured.

Steps.alsoEmpty: Also when the text is empty
Steps.chooseDataset: Choose the dataset to look up

Mappings.intro: Where each target column comes from, in each branch. Open a cell to write its mapping; every branch must fill each column or say why it cannot.
Mappings.reasonPlaceholder: Why this branch cannot provide the column (required)

Consolidation.singleBranch: This model has one branch: there is nothing to consolidate. Add a branch to combine several sources.
Consolidation.intro: How the rows of the branches become one table: stacked, then optionally matched on business keys so that one row survives per entity.
Consolidation.combineHint: Stack the rows of every branch, keeping or removing exact duplicates.
Consolidation.sourceColumnHint: A column that tells which branch each row comes from. Leave empty for none.
Consolidation.matchHint: Rows of different branches with the same values in these columns describe the same entity: one row survives.
Consolidation.survivorshipHint: By default, the value of the first branch in this order wins. Override it column by column below.

strategy.first_not_null: First value that is not null

Consolidation.byOf: Column that dates the value of {column}

Quality.intro: Checks run on the built table. Each one becomes a dbt test; an error stops the run, a warning is reported.
Quality.automaticBody: The grain key ({keys}) is checked as not null and unique: there is nothing to add for it.
Quality.noKey: The model has no grain key yet: mark key columns in the Columns tab to check them automatically.

Reusable.rulesSubtitle: Logic written once and reused in the mappings of every model, with its statement in plain language.
Reusable.mappingsSubtitle: Code lists translated from a source to the target, used by mapping steps and by accepted values checks.
Reusable.newRuleHint: You write its parameters and its logic next.
Reusable.newMappingHint: You enter or paste its values next.
Reusable.noDomain: Add a domain first, in Organization › Domains: every rule and value mapping belongs to one.
Reusable.idHint: Lowercase letters, digits, _ and -. It cannot change later.
Reusable.name: Name
Reusable.statementHint: What the rule means for the business, in plain language.
Reusable.noRuleBody: A business rule holds logic used by several columns, such as a key qualified by its source system.
Reusable.noMappingBody: A value mapping translates codes, such as SAP material types into group categories.
Reusable.deleteBody: It is not used anywhere. Its history is kept.
Reusable.deleteUsedBody: It is used in {count, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}: they will show an error until you change them. Its history is kept.
Reusable.parametersHint: The values the rule receives. In the logic, use them as operands of kind Parameter.
Reusable.logicHint: The steps that compute the result. With one parameter, the first step starts from its value.
Reusable.defaultHint: Used for a value with no entry, when a step asks for it.
Reusable.duplicates: {count, plural, one {# source value appears} other {# source values appear}} more than once: only the first row is kept.
Reusable.tooMany: More than {max} entries: read them from a reference dataset instead.
Reusable.pasteHint: Two columns, source then target, one entry per line (copied cells, or values separated by ; or ,).
Reusable.referenceHint: The values come from two columns of a source dataset, for code lists too long to enter here.

Yaml.hint: The file of this object as the project export contains it. Your edits apply to the forms as soon as the file is valid.
Yaml.readOnly: The file of this object as the project export contains it (read only).
Yaml.notApplied: Not applied yet: the forms keep the last valid version until this is fixed.
Yaml.idLocked: The identifier cannot change here: it stays {id}.

Sql.hint: The dbt model generated for Snowflake from this model, as the project download will contain it. It follows every saved change.
Sql.refreshing: Shown for the last saved version: it follows once your change is saved.
Sql.label: Generated SQL
Sql.blocked: The SQL appears once these errors are fixed:

History.title: History
History.subtitle: Every change to the project, newest first: who changed what and when. Compare any two versions of an object, name a version of the whole project, restore.
History.restoredProject: The project was restored to {name}. Check the problems of the restored objects: references may have changed since.
History.noNamed: No named version yet. Name one before a delivery, to compare with it, download its outputs or come back to it.
History.newNamedHint: It marks the current state of every object of the project. It never changes afterwards.
History.name: Name
History.restoreBody: A new version equal to this one is recorded; nothing of the history is lost, and you can restore the current state again later.
History.comparedWithPrevious: Changes of this version ({date}), compared with the one before
History.comparedWithCurrent: From this version ({date}) to the current state
History.comparedWith: From the version of {from} to the version of {to}
History.restoreProject: Restore the project to this version
History.restoreProjectBody: {changed, plural, =0 {No object} one {# object} other {# objects}} will get back their state of that moment, and {removed, plural, =0 {no object} one {# object created since} other {# objects created since}} will be deleted. Everything stays in the history and can be restored.
History.deleteNamedBody: Only the name goes: every version of the objects stays in the history.
History.sameAsNamed: The project is exactly as it was at this version.
History.sinceCounts: {added, plural, =0 {No object added} one {# object added} other {# objects added}}, {removed, plural, =0 {none removed} other {# removed}}, {changed, plural, =0 {none changed} other {# changed}}.
